items.prose: The three-month 130 call is quoted 0.00 / 0.04. `iv_from_quotes` uses `mid(df)` and a solver that returns NaN where no vol fits.
items.question: What are its `iv_bid`, `iv_mid` and `iv_ask`?

options.why: You priced the mid as 0.02. `mid` returns NaN for a zero bid, and the solver passes NaN through.
A zero bid pins no vol: every vol near 0% prices this call at almost nothing, so the solver returns NaN, not 0%.
The ask, £0.04, is above the call's lower bound of 0, so a vol does fit it.

feedback.correct: Only the ask has a vol.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take each of the three prices in turn.

explain.text: A zero bid has no vol and, by our convention, no mid. The ask, £0.04, is a real price with a vol of 21.6%, an upper end with no lower end.

options.why: You split at the spot, or rounded the forward to 100. 100 is below £100.33, so the put is out of the money.
Parity makes one of them redundant. The fit uses the out-of-the-money side only.
